title: The reproducibility crisis in ML research
bottleneck: A large fraction of published ML results can't be reproduced: code unreleased, hyperparameters unreported, evaluation protocols inconsistent — the Gemini Ultra MMLU controversy showed apples-to-oranges comparisons from mixed CoT@32 versus 5-shot protocols — and only about 16% of safety benchmarks use proper statistical methods. The field advances on claims that may not survive re-examination. Reproducibility checklists and artifact evaluations exist but are weakly enforced by venues and rarely checked.
why_it_blocks: Science that can't be verified isn't science. Irreproducible results waste researcher-years and let weak methods masquerade as progress.
current_state: Reproducibility checklists and artifact evaluations exist but are weakly enforced; incentives still reward novel claims over verified ones. Reward structures still favor publishing novel claims, so researchers invest little in verifying others' results.
